snp5.8:1.1:
There are in the world
sages, they say
snp5.8:1.4:
Do they call one a sage
for possessing knowledge
snp5.8:1.5: or possessing a way of life?
snp5.8:2.1:
The Buddha:
Not on account of his views,
learning,
or knowledge
snp5.8:2.2:
do the skilled here, Nanda,
call one a sage.
snp5.8:2.4:
undesiring,
untroubled:
Those, I say, are called sages.
snp5.8:3.3:
describe purity
in terms of views & learning,
snp5.8:3.4:
describe purity
in terms of habits & practices,
snp5.8:3.5:
describe purity
in terms of manifold ways:
snp5.8:3.6: Have they, dear sir, living there in that way,
snp5.8:3.8:
I ask you, Blessed One.
Please tell me.
snp5.8:4.3:
describe purity
in terms of views & learning,
snp5.8:4.4:
describe purity
in terms of habits & practices,
snp5.8:4.5:
describe purity
in terms of manifold ways:
snp5.8:4.6: None of them, living there in that way,
snp5.8:4.7: I tell you, have crossed over birth & aging.
snp5.8:5.3:
describe purity
in terms of views & learning,
snp5.8:5.4:
describe purity
in terms of habits & practices,
snp5.8:5.5:
describe purity
in terms of manifold ways:
snp5.8:5.6:
If, sage, as you say,
they’ve not crossed over the flood,
snp5.8:5.7:
then who in the world
of beings divine & human,
snp5.8:5.8:
dear sir,
has crossed over birth & aging?
snp5.8:5.9:
I ask you, Blessed One.
Please tell me.
snp5.8:6.1:
The Buddha:
I don’t say that all brahmans & contemplatives
snp5.8:6.5:
what’s seen, heard, & sensed,
habits & practices
—all—
snp5.8:6.6:
who’ve abandoned their manifold ways
—again, all—
snp5.8:6.8:
They are the ones, I tell you,
who’ve crossed over the flood.
snp5.8:7.1:
Nanda:
I relish, Gotama, the Great Seer’s words
snp5.8:7.4:
what’s seen, heard, & sensed,
habits & practices
—all—
snp5.8:7.5:
who’ve abandoned their manifold ways
—again, all—
